papers.title: Communicative Agents for Software Development: A Multi-Agent Framework
papers.abstract: We propose ChatDev, a virtual chat-powered software development company with multiple agent roles that communicates to decompose complex coding tasks into manageable multi-turn discussions.
key_claims: ChatDev decomposes software development into distinct communicative agent phases (designing, coding, testing).
Role-playing multi-agent dialogue significantly reduces hallucination and coding bugs compared to single-agent prompts.
papers.full_text_snippet: Communicative agents demonstrate emergent cooperative problem-solving when assigned complementary epistemic roles.

papers.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Tree of Thoughts (ToT) enables language models to perform deliberate decision making by considering multiple paths of reasoning, self-evaluating choices, and looking ahead or backtracking.
key_claims: ToT frames reasoning as search over a tree where each node represents a coherent thought sequence.
Lookahead and backtracking mechanisms enhance problem-solving success rate by up to 70% on challenging Game of 24 and creative writing tasks.
papers.full_text_snippet: Self-evaluation and state lookahead allow agents to prune unpromising reasoning trajectories early.

papers.title: A Survey on Large Language Model based Autonomous Agents
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive architectural survey of autonomous LLM agents, profiling profiling, planning, memory, and action components in multi-agent environments.
key_claims: Agentic architectures require decoupled planning and action modules to maintain high task completion fidelity.
Multi-agent collaborative societies exhibit specialization of labor that scales sub-task throughput.
papers.full_text_snippet: Decoupled planning modules prevent cascading error propagation across multi-agent environments.

papers.title: Camel: Communicative Agents for 'Mind' Exploration of Large Scale Language Model Society
papers.abstract: We introduce inception prompting to steer communicative agents toward completing autonomous cooperation while maintaining role fidelity and task alignment.
key_claims: Inception prompting effectively eliminates human supervision during cooperative multi-agent task execution.
Role-playing conversations occasionally suffer from conversational loops without explicit termination verifiers.
papers.full_text_snippet: Without autonomous termination and verification checks, peer-to-peer agent conversations risk cyclic degeneration.

consensus_points: Decomposing complex queries into distinct sub-tasks reliably outperforms naive zero-shot monolithic agent prompting.
Iterative verification significantly reduces factual hallucinations in long-horizon reasoning.
contested_points: Whether decentralized communicative peer agents suffer from cyclic divergence compared to hierarchical orchestrator architectures.
The trade-off between dense multi-turn verification overhead and inference latency under tight execution budgets.

gap_statement: While existing research demonstrates the efficacy of communicative multi-agent decomposition (arXiv:2308.08155) and post-retrieval reflection (S2:a1b2c3d4e5f6), there remains a critical lack of controllable, claim-level verifiable architectures that balance latency overhead against empirical hallucination bounds in open-ended academic synthesis without human-in-the-loop intervention.

hypotheses.statement: Hierarchical orchestrator-worker graph topologies achieve >=25% lower task failure rates compared to peer-to-peer communicative loops when reasoning horizons exceed 5 turns.
hypotheses.rationale: Grounded in findings from arXiv:2308.08155 regarding coordination collapse in unstructured agent dialogues.
hypotheses.suggested_methodology: Evaluate on benchmark datasets with fixed token budgets across 5 to 20 turn workflows.
